:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/problem: Given that the determinant of  $\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1 & 2 \\ k & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 3\end{bmatrix}$ is $2,$ find the value of the constant $k.$
:knowledge-point/canonical-example.:question/worked-solution:
Let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $k\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 2 \\ k & 4 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}| & =3|\begin{aligned}4 & 5 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}k & 5 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|+2|\begin{aligned}k & 4 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(12-10)-1(3k-0)+2(2k-0) \\  & =3\cdot 2-1\cdot 3k+2\cdot 2k \\  & =6-3k+4k \\  & =k+6\end{aligned}
$$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $2,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}k+6 & =2 \\ k & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & z \\ z & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =2|\begin{aligned}3 & z \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1|\begin{aligned}2 & z \\ z & 1\end{aligned}|+5|\begin{aligned}2 & 3 \\ z & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2(3+z)-(2-{z}^{2})+5(-2-3z) \\  & =6+2z-2+{z}^{2}-10-15z \\  & ={z}^{2}-13z-6\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1 & 6 & m \\ m & 3 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| & =1|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-6|\begin{aligned}m & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|+m|\begin{aligned}m & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(3-0)-6(m-0)+m(m-6) \\  & =3-6m+{m}^{2}-6m \\  & ={m}^{2}-12m+3\end{aligned}
$$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $-29,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{m}^{2}-12m+3 & =-29 \\ {m}^{2}-12m+32 & =0 \\ m & =\frac{-(-12)\pm \sqrt{{12}^{2}-4\cdot 1\cdot 32}}{2\cdot 1} \\  & =\frac{12\pm \sqrt{16}}{2} \\  & =\frac{12\pm 4}{2} \\  & =6\pm 2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $m=4$ and $m=8.$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Given that
$$
\displaystyle D=\begin{bmatrix}5 & 6 & 2 \\ -8 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 1 & x\end{bmatrix}
$$ 
and $det(D)=481,$ find the value of $x.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $x:$
    

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(D) & =\begin{vmatrix}5 & 6 & 2 \\ -8 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & 1 & x\end{vmatrix} \\  & =5\begin{vmatrix}0 & 5 \\ 1 & x\end{vmatrix}-6\begin{vmatrix}-8 & 5 \\ 3 & x\end{vmatrix}+2\begin{vmatrix}-8 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{vmatrix} \\  & =5\cdot (-5)-6\cdot (-8x-15)+2\cdot (-8) \\  & =-25+48x+90-16 \\  & =48x+49\end{aligned}
$$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $481,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}48x+49 & =481 \\ 48x & =432 \\ x & =9\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem: Given that $B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & -3 & -1 \\ m & 1 & m \\ -1 & 4 & -2\end{bmatrix}$ and $det(B)=-50,$ find the value of $m.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $m:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(B) & =\begin{vmatrix}2 & -3 & -1 \\ m & 1 & m \\ -1 & 4 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =2\begin{vmatrix}1 & m \\ 4 & -2\end{vmatrix}-(-3)\begin{vmatrix}m & m \\ -1 & -2\end{vmatrix}-1\begin{vmatrix}m & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =2\cdot (-2-4m)+3\cdot (-2m+m)-(4m+1) \\  & =-4-8m-3m-4m-1 \\  & =-5-15m\end{aligned}
$$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $-50,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-5-15m & =-50 \\ -15m & =-45 \\ m & =3\end{aligned}
$$

:knowledge-point/questions.:question/problem:
Given that the determinant of 
$$
\displaystyle \begin{bmatrix}1-2p & 4 & 2p+1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 2\end{bmatrix}
$$ 
is $-126,$  find the value of $p.$
:knowledge-point/questions.:question/worked-solution:
Let's use our formula to find an expression for the determinant in terms of $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{vmatrix}1-2p & 4 & 2p+1 \\ 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 6 & -2 & 2\end{vmatrix} & =(1-2p)\begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 \\ -2 & 2\end{vmatrix}-4\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 6 & 2\end{vmatrix}+(2p+1)\begin{vmatrix}1 & 3 \\ 6 & -2\end{vmatrix} \\  & =(1-2p)\cdot 6-4\cdot 2+(2p+1)\cdot (-20) \\  & =6-12p-8-40p-20 \\  & =-52p-22\end{aligned}
$$

Since the determinant of the matrix is $-126,$ we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}-52p-22 & =-126 \\ -52p & =-104 \\ p & =2\end{aligned}
$$
